applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Convention between France and Germany for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1959, as amended)
Convention between France and the United States for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1994, as amended by Protocols of 2006 and 2009)
Convention between France and the United Kingdom for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (2009)
Convention between France and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (2013)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L.561-1 to L.561-57 and R.561-1 et seq.; EU Directive (EU) 2015/849, as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843; Order No. 2016-1635 of 1 December 2016; Decree No. 2018-284 of 18 April 2018; UBO Register (Registre national des bénéficiaires effectifs) established under Decree No. 2017-1094 of 12 June 2017 and Decree No. 2019-315 of 12 April 2019, administered by the commercial court registry (Greffe du Tribunal de commerce) and supervised by INPI; public access restricted under Article L.561-45-1 CMF.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation or equivalent extract of the foreign corporate shareholder (Kbis-equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry in the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of each ultimate beneficial owner and appointed director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or solicitor in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO (utility bill or equivalent, issued within the last 90 days)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, municipal authority, or licensed bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization in non-Hague jurisdictions; no apostille required for Hague signatory states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and proof of funds for the initial capital contribution
Power of attorney executed abroad authorizing the French incorporation agent (if applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of execution

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all UBOs, directors, and signatories against the French national asset-freeze list (Fichier des personnes et entités sanctionnées, Direction Générale du Trésor), the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, and the OFAC SDN List as a banking best-practice benchmark; enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (PEPs) as defined by FATF Recommendation 12 and Article L.561-10 CMF; ongoing transaction monitoring and re-screening obligations under Articles L.561-12 and L.561-13 CMF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), operated by INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle); name availability search through the Registre National des Entreprises and the Infogreffe database of the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in the Latin alphabet. French-language naming is preferred and mandatory for all statutory publications; foreign words are permitted provided the liability designation 'SAS' or 'société par actions simplifiée' is appended. Transliteration into non-Latin scripts is not recognized for registration. The name must comply with Article L.123-1 of the Code de commerce, must not be contrary to public order or morality, and must not infringe prior registered trademarks or business names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may immediately refile an amended name proposal through the Guichet Unique. A formal administrative remedy is available by lodging a written complaint with the INPI Direction des Relations avec les Usagers within two months of the rejection decision; if the complaint is unsuccessful, a contentious appeal may be filed before the Tribunal judiciaire de Paris or the competent commercial court, with a final cascation option before the Cour de cassation; representation by a French avocat is strongly advised.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for registration purposes. The SAS may domicile its registered office at the legal representative's personal residence for up to five years (Article L.123-10 Code de commerce) or at a licensed commercial domiciliation provider (Articles L.123-11-2 et seq. Code de commerce). For the ISIC 7420 stock-photo and AI visual assets business, a virtual office is acceptable provided that accounting records, statutory minute books, and AML/CFT documentation remain physically accessible on demand and that sufficient economic substance (revenue-generating contracts, bank accounts, administrative management) is demonstrable for tax residence purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified risk: approximately 15-25% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 18 months of operation where the registered office is a professional domiciliation address, increasing to approximately 30-40% where the office is the legal representative's personal residence; URSSAF and DGFiP inspections are generally announced in advance except in cases of suspected fraud or AML/CFT integrity breaches; no sector-specific physical presence mandate applies to ISIC 7420.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance search and reservation certificate (Guichet Unique / INPI)
Registration in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), including issuance of Kbis extract
Publication of the incorporation notice in a Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per paid insert line

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting and legal review of the SAS Articles of Association (statuts) by a French avocat
UBO declaration (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) filing with the RCS
Apostille and notarization of foreign corporate shareholder documents and powers of attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public and competent authority of the document's country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular statutory tariff and notarial fee benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT onboarding protocol: PEP and sanctions screening software, risk rating, and UBO verification setup

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code, Articles L. 210-1 et seq. (commercial companies) and L. 227-1 to L. 227-20-1 (SAS); applicable formation and registration provisions include Articles R. 123-1 et seq. and R. 123-53 et seq.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) for the mandatory Guichet unique des formalités d’entreprises; the competent commercial court registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce) records the company in the Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic company-formation formalité submitted through the Guichet unique, supported by the signed articles of association (statuts), with the required declaration of beneficial owners (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: A SAS has no statutory minimum share capital; capital may be set in the articles. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid at incorporation, with the balance payable within five years. Cash contributions must be deposited before filing with an authorized bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; deposited funds are released after presentation of the RCS registration certificate (extrait Kbis). The USD filing-fee figure is an approximate conversion of standard registry and beneficial-owner filing charges; fees are set in euros and may change.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company’s articles of association, as executed by the subscribers, are approved and that the shares specified therein are accepted as subscribed, subject to payment in accordance with the articles and applicable law. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at [full French address]. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [name] is appointed President (Président) of the Company for an indefinite term, with authority to represent and bind the Company within the powers conferred by law and the articles. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [name] is appointed [Director/other officer, if applicable]. The President is authorized to complete registration formalities, obtain the Kbis, and take incidental implementation actions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the SAS articles and determine capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company subscribers; an authorized bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations for cash-capital deposits
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare articles stating the company name, purpose, registered office, duration, capital, share allocation, governance, and appointment method for the President. Obtain signatures from all subscribers. Deposit at least 50% of each cash contribution and obtain a certificate of deposit. A notarial deed is not generally required for ordinary cash contributions; notarization or other formalities may apply to particular in-kind contributions, especially contributions involving real property.
required_dossiers: Identity and address details of each subscriber
Valuation report for in-kind contributions, unless a statutory exemption validly applies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistent articles, subscriber details, or deposit amounts; obtain a corrected deposit certificate and re-execute amended articles where required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized legal-announcement journal (journal d’annonces légales) in the département of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the prescribed SAS formation notice after execution of the articles. Ensure it states the company name, legal form, capital, registered-office address, corporate purpose, duration, President’s identity and address, and the relevant RCS registration details. Retain the publication certificate for the electronic filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a corrected notice and publication certificate if mandatory particulars are missing or inconsistent; upload the corrected evidence with the filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the company-formation filing and beneficial-owner declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités d’entreprises; registration is processed by the competent greffe du tribunal de commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the creation formalité electronically through the Guichet unique. Upload the signed articles, capital-deposit certificate, publication certificate, registered-office evidence, President’s identification and non-conviction declaration, and any required authority or immigration documents. Complete the beneficial-owner declaration and pay the applicable euro-denominated filing charges. Respond promptly to any request for supplementation.
required_dossiers: President’s identity document and non-conviction declaration
Power of attorney, if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Review the Guichet unique deficiency notice, correct or supplement the identified item within the stated deadline, and resubmit through the portal. If refused, use the applicable registry review or appeal procedure stated in the decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent greffe du tribunal de commerce and the capital-deposit institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the company’s SIREN/SIRET identifiers, RCS registration evidence, and Kbis extract after approval. Provide the Kbis or other requested registration evidence to the depositary to release the paid-up capital into the company account. Maintain the statutory registers and retain the formation records at the registered office.
required_dossiers: RCS registration confirmation and Kbis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, check the portal status and respond to registry requests. If capital release is refused, provide the depositary with the Kbis and matching company and account particulars.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board or manufacturing authority approval is ordinarily required for an online stock-photography marketplace or generative visual-assets platform.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sector-specific operating or manufacturing permit is ordinarily required for the stated digital-platform activity. Separate approvals may apply to regulated ancillary activities or a physical facility.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition écologique; environmental screening and permitting are administered by the competent regional or departmental authorities, including the Direction régionale de l’environnement, de l’aménagement et du logement (DREAL), as applicable.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Ordinarily exempt from project EIA for a digital marketplace without an industrial installation or qualifying development project. Screening is required if the company later undertakes a project listed under the French Environmental Code or operates an installation subject to environmental permitting.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industry-specific wastewater, VOC, or industrial-waste thresholds ordinarily apply to the stated online activity. Any premises must comply with applicable general rules, including authorized wastewater discharge, waste-sorting and disposal requirements, and any site-specific environmental permit or ICPE requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No manufacturing-site clearance is ordinarily required for a digital-only business. For leased or occupied premises, comply with applicable building and fire-safety rules; premises open to the public may require ERP authorization and fire-safety review. Employers must meet French occupational health and safety duties, including risk assessment in the document unique d’évaluation des risques professionnels (DUERP), and obtain any building-specific structural approvals required for the premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP), through the competent Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and the official impots.gouv.fr portal. French VAT identification and tax-account procedures are administered by the competent SIE; non-established businesses generally deal with the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE) where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS obtains its SIREN and SIRET identifiers through registration with the competent business-registration authority and the Registre national des entreprises, with information transmitted to the DGFiP. The company must file the applicable tax-registration information, identify its principal establishment, business activities, accounting period, beneficial ownership and bank details, and request VAT activation or a French VAT number from the competent SIE. The French VAT number is generally formatted as FR plus a two-character key and the nine-digit SIREN. A non-resident entity carrying out taxable transactions in France must assess whether French VAT registration is required, whether it may use the VAT One Stop Shop, and whether it must appoint a French tax representative. Businesses established in another EU Member State generally do not require a French fiscal representative solely because they are VAT-registered in France; businesses established outside the European Union may require an accredited French fiscal representative unless an applicable mutual-assistance arrangement or special rule applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). Subject to statutory eligibility conditions, including limits on age, workforce, turnover or balance-sheet size, and ownership requirements, certain SAS entities may elect temporary taxation under personal income tax (impôt sur le revenu), generally for a maximum period of five fiscal years. This is an entity-level statutory election and not a United States-style check-the-box election. No general French check-the-box election is available. French anti-hybrid-mismatch rules may deny deductions or impose inclusion where arrangements produce deduction/non-inclusion or double-deduction outcomes, but they do not constitute an elective entity-classification regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: French value added tax (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA), harmonized with the European Union VAT Directive.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: France applies a VAT franchise regime rather than a single universal registration threshold. For domestic businesses principally supplying services, the ordinary franchise threshold is generally EUR 37,500 of annual turnover, with a tolerance threshold generally of EUR 41,250, subject to the applicable year and legislative changes. For trading, accommodation and comparable goods activities, the principal threshold is generally EUR 85,000, with a tolerance threshold generally of EUR 93,500. Special thresholds apply to certain regulated professions and activities. The threshold does not protect a business from VAT obligations arising from reverse charge, intra-Community acquisitions, imports, distance sales, platform rules, or transactions for which French VAT is otherwise due. A foreign business without a French establishment may require French VAT registration from its first taxable transaction where no exemption, reverse charge, One Stop Shop or other simplification applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France does not currently operate a universal real-time invoice-clearance system for all private-sector transactions. Mandatory domestic business-to-business electronic invoicing is scheduled to apply in phases: all businesses must be able to receive compliant electronic invoices from 1 September 2026; large and mid-sized businesses must issue them from 1 September 2026; and small and micro-enterprises must issue them from 1 September 2027, subject to legislative or administrative changes. Invoices must generally pass through an approved private platform or the designated public infrastructure under the applicable reform. Electronic transaction reporting (e-reporting) will apply to specified business-to-consumer and cross-border transactions. Public-sector invoicing is generally handled through the Chorus Pro system. France does not impose a universal digital tax stamp or real-time fiscal clearance requirement for ordinary commercial invoices, although electronic-format, authenticity, integrity, archiving and audit-trail requirements apply.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods dispatched from France to a destination outside the European Union may be supplied free of French VAT where the exporter can substantiate exportation and comply with customs and invoicing requirements. The principal evidence is the electronic customs export record and confirmation that the goods exited the European Union. Intra-Community supplies of goods may generally be exempt from French VAT where the customer is identified for VAT in another Member State, the supplier reports the transaction correctly, and transport to that Member State is evidenced. Services supplied to a business customer established outside France are generally taxed according to the place-of-supply rules and may be outside the scope of French VAT rather than technically zero-rated; evidence of the customer's business status, establishment and contractual delivery location is required. Digital stock-media, licensing and generative-asset services require separate analysis because B2B and B2C place-of-supply, electronically supplied service, marketplace-intermediary and platform-deemed-supplier rules may differ.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic customs export declaration containing the Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Electronic confirmation of exit from the European Union or equivalent customs exit evidence
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, value, currency, Incoterms and export destination
Transport documentation, such as bill of lading, airway bill, CMR consignment note or courier proof of delivery
Packing list and, where relevant, import-clearance or delivery evidence in the destination country
Proof of the customer's location and VAT status for intra-Community transactions, where applicable
Contract, order, delivery and payment records supporting the commercial substance of the transaction
Bank remittance evidence where relevant to refund or audit substantiation; France does not generally require an inward-remittance certificate as a universal export-VAT condition
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general foreign-exchange repatriation deadline requiring export proceeds to be brought into France within 180 days. Export proceeds may generally be received through ordinary banking channels subject to anti-money-laundering, customs, accounting and payment-reporting rules. Incorrectly applying an exemption or zero rate can result in assessment of the unpaid French VAT, statutory late-payment interest, and tax penalties. The standard penalty for failure to pay or late payment is generally 5% of the tax due, with late-payment interest generally accruing at the statutory rate, subject to applicable procedural rules. In cases involving deliberate misstatement, concealment or fraudulent conduct, increased penalties may apply, potentially reaching 40% for deliberate default and 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abusive conduct, in addition to recovery of VAT, interest, and possible criminal exposure for serious tax fraud. A VAT refund may be denied or clawed back where export proof is incomplete, inconsistent, fabricated or not retained for the statutory record-retention period. Customs penalties, import-export adjustment, platform reporting consequences and joint-liability rules may also apply where the transaction involves an intermediary or deemed supplier.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, operating within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank. Applicable foreign-exchange, payment-services, sanctions, and anti-money-laundering rules also derive from European Union law and French legislation administered by competent authorities including the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution, the Autorité des marchés financiers, the Direction générale du Trésor, and TRACFIN.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro, which is fully convertible for ordinary current-account and capital-account transactions. There is no general French exchange-control approval for dividends, interest, royalties, service fees, loan repayments, capital contributions, or liquidation proceeds paid to non-residents. Transfers remain subject to corporate-law distribution rules, applicable withholding tax, transfer-pricing and beneficial-ownership requirements, sanctions screening, anti-money-laundering controls, and documentary evidence of the underlying transaction. A non-resident shareholder may subscribe for SAS shares and pay share capital or share premium through a French bank, provided source of funds, ownership, tax residence, and transaction-purpose information are satisfactory. Certain foreign investments in protected French sectors may require prior filing or authorization under French foreign-investment-control rules; a stock photography and generative visual-assets marketplace is not ordinarily a protected strategic sector solely by reason of its business description, but technology, data, defense, or critical-infrastructure features must be separately assessed.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to a domestic bank, convert foreign-currency export receipts into euros, or repatriate them within a prescribed period. Export receipts may be maintained in foreign-currency accounts, subject to the bank's account terms, accounting records, sanctions controls, and tax compliance. Cross-border payment reporting may be performed by banks or payment service providers for statistical, regulatory, and anti-money-laundering purposes. Exporters must retain commercial invoices, contracts, transport or delivery evidence, customs records where applicable, and payment reconciliation records. Cash or equivalent monetary instruments of EUR 10,000 or more entering or leaving the European Union must be declared to customs. No mandatory conversion ratio applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and the relevant Crédit Agricole regional bank
Banque Populaire or Caisse d'Epargne entity within Groupe BPCE

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for operating receipts, card acquiring, SEPA payments, and multi-currency treasury if the provider is an EU-authorized payment institution or electronic-money institution passporting into France. Low for statutory share-capital escrow, primary corporate-banking functions, cash-intensive activity, or transactions involving elevated sanctions and source-of-funds risk. Offshore digital EMIs without EU authorization, passporting, or a French or EEA regulated partner should not be used for regulated payment services to the SAS. Stripe and PayPal may support collections and payouts subject to their merchant underwriting, reserve, prohibited-business, chargeback, and beneficial-owner policies; they should not be treated as substitutes for a regulated corporate bank account. Customer funds held by an EMI are generally safeguarded rather than covered by the French deposit-guarantee scheme applicable to eligible bank deposits.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that every director physically attend a bank branch. Remote onboarding may be permitted where the bank can complete reliable identity verification, beneficial-owner identification, documentary authentication, management verification, and risk assessment. Bank policy may nevertheless require a video interview, certified copies, French or EU address evidence, wet-ink or qualified electronic signatures, a local signatory, or an in-person meeting for a newly incorporated SAS, non-resident directors, complex ownership, high-risk countries, unusual payment flows, or capital escrow. The bank may require the certificate of deposit and corporate documents before releasing subscribed capital after registration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recently incorporated SAS with no operating history, no French trading footprint, or an incomplete post-incorporation file.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed articles of association; certificate of incorporation or current extrait Kbis; certificate of beneficial ownership filing; registered-office evidence; board or shareholder resolution approving accounts and signatories; business plan; 12-month cash-flow forecast; customer and supplier contracts; website and platform description; expected monthly transaction profile; tax registrations where applicable; and explanation of the initial funding timetable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder, director, or ultimate beneficial owner; opaque holding chain; nominee arrangement; or ownership through multiple jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry extracts for every holding entity; ownership chart to each natural-person beneficial owner; passports and residential-address evidence; tax-residence certificates; directors' registers; shareholder registers; powers of attorney; source-of-wealth statements; source-of-funds evidence; and written explanation of control rights and economic ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or unexplained capital contribution, shareholder loan, intercompany transfer, or payment from an account held by a third party.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription agreement or loan agreement; shareholder or board approval; bank statements showing the originating account; audited or management accounts of the funder; sale-of-asset or investment evidence where relevant; payment reference identifying the SAS; beneficial-owner confirmation; and reconciliation between the amount received and the accounting entry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business model involving artificial intelligence, user-generated content, digital assets, licensing, or high volumes of international micro-payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed product and platform description; intellectual-property ownership or license chain; content-moderation and takedown procedures; customer terms; privacy and data-protection documentation; sanctions and prohibited-country controls; payment-flow diagram; merchant-of-record analysis; chargeback and refund policy; expected jurisdictions; and evidence that the activity is not gambling, adult content, unlicensed financial services, crypto-asset dealing, or another prohibited category.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk geography, sanctioned counterparty, adverse media, politically exposed person, or mismatch between declared activity and payment counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due-diligence memorandum; independent adverse-media results; PEP and sanctions screening records; transaction-purpose evidence; end-customer and beneficial-owner information; legal sanctions analysis; compliance approval; documentary proof of goods or services; and senior-management authorization for exceptional transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected payments through Stripe, PayPal, or other PSPs inconsistent with the stated business, including rapid pass-through, unusually high refunds, or multi-currency settlement anomalies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PSP contracts; merchant underwriting approval; payment-flow and settlement reports; invoices; customer geography; refund and chargeback statistics; reconciliation controls; reserve terms; fraud-monitoring procedures; segregation of operating and client-money flows where applicable; and monthly management reporting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient French tax, accounting, payroll, or regulatory substance for the stated operating scale.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Engagement letter with French accountant; accounting-system evidence; VAT registration or documented non-registration basis; tax filings where available; payroll and employment records; lease or domiciliation agreement; insurance certificates; supplier and customer invoices; and explanation of outsourced functions and decision-making location.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Requests for cash withdrawals, payments to personal accounts, third-party settlement accounts, or transfers lacking a clear commercial purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written transaction rationale; invoice or agreement; beneficiary ownership evidence; board approval where material; sanctions and AML review; payment authorization matrix; supporting delivery or performance evidence; and documented prohibition of personal-account settlement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route share capital and share-premium funding from the subscriber's own verified bank account to the French bank's dedicated capital-escrow account before incorporation or capital increase. Use a clear payment reference such as 'subscription for shares in [SAS name]—share capital' or 'share premium contribution' and identify the subscriber and corporate registration process. Provide the bank with the signed articles, subscription form, shareholder resolution, ownership chart, source-of-funds evidence, and expected amount. After incorporation or the capital increase, deliver the Kbis and required corporate documents so the depositary bank can release funds to the operational account. Shareholder loans and ordinary intercompany funding should be sent to the operational account under a documented loan or cash-pooling arrangement, with arm's-length terms and accounting treatment. SEPA Credit Transfer is generally preferred for euro-denominated EEA transfers; SWIFT cross-border wires should include the correct beneficiary legal name, IBAN, BIC, registered address, purpose narrative, and any bank-requested regulatory information. France does not use a universal statutory purpose-code system for ordinary corporate wires, so the commercial purpose and supporting documents must be accurate and consistent. Banks may report statistical or regulatory data and may suspend or reject incomplete, sanctioned, or unexplained transfers.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the SEPA area, subject to bank limits and sanctions screening. Use SWIFT MT103 terminology for cross-border customer credit transfers, recognizing that ISO 20022 messages are increasingly used in bank infrastructures; include complete originator, beneficiary, invoice, currency, amount, and purpose information. For documentary trade, use a commercial letter of credit under UCP 600, preferably confirmed where counterparty or country risk justifies confirmation, and require compliant documents such as commercial invoice, transport document, insurance evidence, packing list, and certificate of origin where applicable. Documentary collections may be processed under URC 522. Maintain segregation between supplier payments, shareholder distributions, payroll, taxes, refunds, and platform settlements. Screen all counterparties and banks against applicable EU and UN sanctions and retain invoices, contracts, proof of delivery or service performance, customs records where applicable, and payment reconciliations. For platform payouts, use PSP settlement accounts only under documented merchant agreements and reconcile gross receipts, fees, refunds, chargebacks, reserves, and net settlement to the French ledger.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable euro/foreign-currency forwards entered into with an authorized bank or investment firm for identified forecast or committed exposures, documented under an appropriate master agreement and supported by a treasury policy.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies subject to local convertibility or settlement restrictions, provided the counterparty is authorized, the transaction is used for genuine commercial hedging, and applicable local-market rules, reporting, and net-settlement requirements are satisfied.

Cross-currency swaps or currency swaps for identified shareholder loans, bank debt, lease liabilities, or recurring operating exposures, with maturity, notional, valuation, collateral, and termination terms documented.

Foreign-exchange options and collars may be used for hedging where the cost, premium, accounting treatment, suitability, and counterparty documentation are approved; avoid speculative or leveraged structures unrelated to the SAS's underlying exposures.

Spot foreign-exchange conversions through the operating bank or authorized payment institution for ordinary settlement needs, with competitive-rate controls, dual authorization, and transaction-level reconciliation.

Apply EMIR-related requirements where applicable, including legal entity identification, trade confirmation, portfolio reconciliation, risk-mitigation procedures, collateral arrangements, and clearing or reporting analysis. Maintain evidence that derivatives are risk-reducing and proportionate to forecast revenue, supplier, debt, or dividend exposures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholder meeting (Assemblée Générale Ordinaire) approving the annual accounts, management report and, where applicable, dividend allotment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SAS corporate file / shareholders register (minutes kept at the registered office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of each corporate fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct registry penalty, but any shareholder may petition the Commercial Court for the appointment of a meeting convenor; persistent non-approval prevents lawful filing of accounts and exposes directors to civil liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of the annual statutory accounts (comptes annuels) and related documents with the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registry of the Commercial Court / RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval and no later than seven months after the fiscal year end; the registry may extend the deadline only in exceptional cases
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit may result in an injunction order with daily fine (astreinte), an administrative fine up to EUR 7,500 for a legal person, and repeated non-deposit can trigger court-ordered strike-off from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Updated declaration of beneficial owners (déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs) and annual UBO register verification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any change in beneficial ownership; the corporate secretary confirms the UBO register at the annual maintenance date even when no filing event occurs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to register UBO changes or submission of inaccurate data is punishable by fines for the legal entity (up to EUR 15,000 per false statement in aggravated cases) and may be treated as a registry obstacle to subsequent corporate filings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: French corporate income tax return (Liasse fiscale, form 2065 series) and annual corporate income tax (IS) balance payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP), corporate tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December year-end, the return must go online by the second working day after 15 May of the following year; for any other fiscal year-end, the return and balance are due within three months after the close of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing adds a 10% penalty to the corporate income tax liability; late payment accrues at 5% plus monthly statutory interest (0.2% per month), and systematic default can give rise to additional recovery measures by the tax claims department

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business property tax return and payment of the Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises (CFE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFIP local tax office (Service des Impôts des Entreprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: CFE is determined annually and payable by the 15th of December of the year of assessment; declaration obligations follow the blocking of the prior-year base and event changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid CFE attracts a 10% late-payment penalty plus 0.2% monthly interest; onward recovery can include liens on business assets and remise denial

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) must be appointed by the SAS when, for at least two consecutive fiscal years, the company exceeds two of the following three thresholds: balance sheet total higher than EUR 4,000,000, net turnover excluding tax higher than EUR 8,000,000, or an average of more than 50 permanently employed persons. The obligation also applies when the entity controls one or more French subsidiaries and submits consolidated accounts, or when required by specific regulations (banking, insurance, crowdfunding, listed title issuers, certain group situations).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French local GAAP, principally the accounting plan set by Regulation ANC 2014-03 and the French Accounting Code; the SAS is not permitted to draw up its individual annual accounts under IFRS. Consolidated accounts, when required by the Commercial Code, may follow IFRS for listed groups or groups with publicly traded debt.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each year-end, before the annual shareholder meeting, the corporate secretary must reconcile the SAS share register, directorships, legal representative data, and bank mandate list against the RCS extract and the beneficial-owner register. Any discrepancy is corrected by a new registry filing within 30 days of the triggering event; no renewal filing is due if all beneficial-owner data remains unchanged. The register of beneficial owners must be kept at the registered office and be made available to authorities upon request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (share register / register of securities movements)
Register of Directors and supervisory board deliberations
Minute Book of shareholders' meetings and board resolutions
Register of Beneficial Owners (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 620 – 1,450 (EUR 540 – 1,280) per year for a commercial registered office or corporate agent outside/inside Paris
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,500 – 16,500 (EUR 5,800 – 14,500) for a standard annual statutory audit of a small or mid-size SAS; not payable if the audit mandate thresholds are not triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on first EUR 38,120 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs; Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30%; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) at 30% of eligible innovation expenditure up to EUR 400,000; patent box deduction at 10% for qualifying income from licensed IP
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No time limit; annual utilisation capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1,000,000; optional carryback up to 3 years capped at EUR 1,000,000

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (with annex schedules 2050-2059-W), filed electronically via EDI-EFI platform through impots.gouv.fr professional portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual income tax return; quarterly CIT instalments due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December, with final balance payable upon filing
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal years ending 31 December, filing deadline is the second business day after 1 May (normally 3 May). For off-calendar fiscal years, the return must be lodged within three months of the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting result before tax adjustments; the starting point of the French tax reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident SAS with a French permanent establishment reports French GAAP accounts and reconciles them to home country books; evidence of PE limitation is placed in box 315

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible charges: fines, excessive depreciation, non-arm's-length fees, disallowed provisions and allocations for mandataires sociaux
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back any service or royalty charge from a non-resident related party not supported by a written contract and OECD transfer pricing analysis

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax deductions not recorded in accounting result: CIR credit, patent box deduction, earn-out provisions and special depreciation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must attach calculations and, if treaty preferential tax treatment is claimed, annex the explicit election and residence certificate

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before loss relief and preferential rate application
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter French-source PE profit only; do not include foreign-source profits unless the double tax treaty attributes them to France

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year utilisation of carried-forward losses capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of excess
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses may be deducted only if they economically belong to the French PE and no legal ownership change blocks the carryforward under Article 221-5 CGI

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declares transactions with overseas related enterprises: nature, amount, method and penalties
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory when annual pre-tax turnover exceeds EUR 50 million; a non-resident parent company must still complete it through its French fiscal representative

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge: 10% if filed within 30 days of deadline; 40% if later; 80% if materially false or deliberately omitted. Late-payment interest accrues at 0.20% per month. Non-electronic filing attracts EUR 150 fine. Omission of the TP information statement carries EUR 15,000 penalty per statement; failure to produce master/local file on audit adds 5% of reassessed income.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% withholding under Article 119 bis CGI for dividends paid by a French company to non-resident beneficial owners; reduced to 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where holding is at least 10% for two continuous years or under most French DTAs to 5%, 10% or 15%
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The dividend recipient delivers to the paying company a signed copy of its French residence-certificate form (Cerfa 5000 series) or other official tax residence certificate issued by its competent authority, together with a beneficial-ownership and holding-period declaration, before the payment date; the payer applies the treaty rate on that basis. If treaty relief was wrongly withheld, the recipient may file a claim for restitution with the French tax office before 31 December of the second year following the year of payment, attaching the same residence certificate and proof of entitlement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: domestic WHT at 33.33% under Article 182 B CGI when the non-resident recipient has no French PE; treaty rates commonly 0%, 5% or 10%; EU Interest/Royalties Directive grants 0% for qualifying affiliated companies with at least 25% shareholding held for 24 months. Interest: France applies no domestic WHT on arm's-length corporate interest paid abroad; certain shareholder debt returns may be recharacterised as dividends under thin capitalisation rules; treaty source rates, if any, normally cap at 10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full Master File/Local File documentation is mandatory when French annual turnover or total balance-sheet assets exceed EUR 400 million; annual TP information statement on form 2257-SD is required once annual turnover exceeds EUR 50 million
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France uses the arm's-length principle under Article 57 CGI and the general anti-abuse rule under Article L64 LPF. There is no standalone offshore ESR regime, but an SAS is expected to have real staff, premises, decision-making, assets and commercial risk in France. Absence of substance indicates sham arrangements, leading to reattribution of income, denial of DTA relief under the Principal Purpose Test and potential CFC inclusion for the foreign shareholder.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional concealment of stock-photo or AI-licensing receipts, false accounting entries, undisclosed PayPal/Stripe proceeds, negative invoices or fictitious counterparties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to EUR 500,000 and five years' imprisonment under Article 1741 CGI; increased to EUR 1,000,000 and seven years for organised fraud; administrative fraud penalty of 40% or 80% of omitted tax base plus 0.20% monthly late-payment interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal criminal conviction, confiscation of assets, prohibition to manage, French travel ban and civil liability for restoring hidden profits; the corporate veil may be pierced under Article L267 LPF to recover entity tax debts from directors acting in deliberate bad faith

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Absence of annual TP statement, failure to prepare master/local file, or non-arm's-length cross-border royalty/licensing fees paid by the French SAS or charged to an affiliated stock agency
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: EUR 15,000 penalty for omitted TP statement; reassessment under Article 57 CGI for hidden profit transfers; 5% increase on tax deficit for unavailable documentation; 40% penalty for gross negligence and 0.2% monthly interest thereafter
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly structured non-real service fees are jointly liable for the tax deficiency; travel bans and exclusion from public contracts may be ordered in serious cases; criminal fraud charges may apply if TP documentation is forged

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the French SAS without actual commercial substance: postbox address, nominee directors, no payroll, no local bank account, or routing profits to a zero-tax foreign licensee solely to obtain treaty benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of Article L64 LPF (abus de droit) to disregard the sham and reassess shareholder-level distributions; 80% abusive arrangement penalty; refusal of treaty relief under the Principal Purpose Test; nullification of advantageous tax positions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: De facto managers may be held personally liable for French taxes, penalties and interest; the court may impose a travel ban, order civil restitution of distributed profits and permit a criminal fraud indictment when the sham was the instrument of the offence

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Funnelling marketplace payments through personal PayPal/Stripe accounts, commingling customer subscription funds with director assets, refusing transparency on beneficial owners, or executing cash flows to sanctioned jurisdictions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 324-1 French Penal Code: five years' imprisonment and EUR 375,000 fine, increased to ten years and EUR 750,000 when habitual; corrective tax reassessment plus 80% penalty; asset freezing and confiscation orders
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face criminal conviction, travel bans and asset seizure; the corporate veil is disregarded for the laundering instrument, and shareholders must demonstrate legitimate origin of distributed funds or restitution
